Elisabeth was speaking to me in front of a row of smashed shop windows, shattered glass still littering the tree-lined Parisian street. Its walls were daubed with red-lettered graffiti insulting French police and signed with the date of the riots, 17 October. I'd stopped Elisabeth and her friend to ask their thoughts on what happened on Saturday. Elisabeth was so upset that, when she spoke, she seemed close to tears. "My friend thinks this is civil war in France but I don't. Saturday is about something else entirely." But what did happen exactly? Who was behind the riots? French media have played and replayed a video shot on Saturday showing groups of young men dressed in black, with a black, folded kerchief around their face to hide their identity, apparently attacking a number of police vans with what look like large hammers or machetes. Get hands-free personalized help on the road with Gemini
clusters.text: Google is bringing Personal Intelligence to Gemini AI in your car. With this update, Gemini in Android Auto and cars with Google built-in can tap into your information across Google apps, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube, and Search. As an example, Google says you can ask Gemini about your flight status if you’re driving to the airport. The AI assistant can pull your flight details from a confirmation message in Gmail and then use that information to look up the status. You can also ask Gemini to “take me to my doctor’s appointment” instead of pulling up directions manually, or ask it to “find the car wash from the photo I took last week and navigate there.” [Video: Personal Intelligence in cars] Google brought its Gemini assistant to Android Auto last year before rolling it out to cars with Google built-in in April. Several carmakers—including Ford, GM, Honda, Nissan, Volvo, and Polestar—have shipped newer cars with Google built-in, which adds support for native Android apps. Google says it will connect your apps to Gemini only if you enable its Personal Intelligence setting. It will also share personalized responses only if you have your phone connected to your car. “If you don’t use Personal Intelligence, everything in the car still works: You can use navigation, listen to music, make calls, and ask questions, but the answers won’t be tailored to you,” Google says. Personal Intelligence is rolling out to Android Auto today, with support coming to cars with Google built-in in the coming months.

clusters.text: In its third-quarter earnings report release on Tuesday, streaming giant Netflix beat many expectations, but still delivered some unwanted news to investors: viewer metrics, especially in the United States, could be better. In the report, the company reported its slowest revenue increase in years, and also revised its outlook for the year, particularly upsetting investors by saying that it is now expecting $2.7 billion in ad revenue instead of the previously projected $3 billion. Netflix’s position as the leading subscription-based streaming service worldwide has done little to quell investor fears that it is losing viewers to the likes of YouTube and TikTok. Its stock was down more than 40% this past year, per WSJ. The slide began when Netflix announced its now-failed intention to buy Warner Bros. Discovery , which is now a part of David Ellison’s Skydance instead . The latest earnings report didn’t necessarily help that downward trend by sending the stock down almost 6%. Going into the report, investors were already worried about viewer metrics, and specifically something called view hours growth, the amount of time viewers spend watching stuff on Netflix. Executives addressed the investors’ concerns that view hours growth was slowing down on Tuesday, and vowed to up the numbers, particularly by revamping its programming in the United States. Netflix’s programming quality has been the source of intense criticism , particularly online . “I know that we could do better, and we want to build on that momentum,” Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos said in the company’s earnings call. “Now we’ve seen an opportunity to take our slate to the next level, especially in the U.S. where we can have an outsized impact when we create a big buzzy show that members love and talk about all over the world.” That content overhaul seemingly has already started with a major restructuring decision. The streaming giant announced last week that it was laying off around 1,000 employees in what is the company’s largest headcount reduction in roughly four years. Key programming chiefs, including Netflix’s chief content officer Bela Bajaria and head of its film unit Dan Lin, were also ousted. A Variety report from Monday claims that Lin had clashed with actor-director Ben Affleck over the use of AI in his latest Netflix release. clusters.text: Crude oil prices ticked higher earlier today, extending gains from Tuesday as traders continued to worry about the stability of flows out of the Middle East. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $110.30 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate at $99.12 per barrel, both up by over 1% from Tuesday. The latest inventory report out of the U.S. contributed to the bullish sentiment with another sizable draw estimated for last week. The rally also comes despite a Wall Street Journal report from Tuesday that said oil flows out of the Middle East had topped pre-war levels in the week to October 18, running at a daily average of 24 million barrels. The report cited data from Kpler, which Reuters had cited in a separate report as estimating Hormuz flows specifically at 8.5 million barrels daily, because of intensified Iranian attacks. For the WSJ report, the Hormuz flows were estimated at 14 million barrels daily. "We believe this is a mix of profit taking and optimistic hopes of a Qatar- or Pakistan-brokered deal, countered by the realisation that any deal is still very distant and compounded further by inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute API, which shows drawdowns continuing in the US for both crude and products,” DBS analyst Suvro Sarkar said, as quoted by Reuters earlier today. Record-breaking freight rates for the Persian Gulf are compounding the price problem in oil. As ING commodity strategists wrote in a Tuesday note, the record rates come from “less efficient use of tankers due to developments in the Middle East”. This is most likely a reference to the surge in ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman as a way of reducing the danger of drone or missile strikes on larger vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. clusters.text: The Independent Football Regulator (IFR) will have “absolute power” to force Manchester City’s owners to sell if they are ultimately found to have run the club improperly, the watchdog’s chair has said. Manchester City have been found guilty of circumventing Premier League rules by an independent commission, which found they set up “sham” commercial arrangements to inflate revenues or reduce costs by over £900m over a nine-season period. They were also found to have made “concerted efforts” to “stop and frustrate” the Premier League’s investigation into those arrangements. City have lodged an appeal, claiming the verdict “contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe”. David Kogan, the chair of the IFR, told podcast The Rest Is Football it was premature to talk about any action his organisation might take while the appeal was ongoing. Kogan did confirm, though, that the IFR had “absolute power” to force a sale by the club’s ownership, if that was felt to be appropriate. “We have the power to ask an owner to step away from a club if we believe that they run a club in a way that is neither fit, fair or done with propriety,” Kogan said. Asked if an owner could refuse to divest, Kogan replied: “No, no, no. We’ve got absolute power to do so.” On the possibility of the IFR investigating City, Kogan said: “I am not going to get pushed into making any judgement on this until we’ve seen all of those questions being answered. Then we will have to decide whether we’re going to mount our own investigation and come to a conclusion on that and what we’re going to do. And pre-empting that would be a colossal mistake.” Manchester City are majority-owned by Abu Dhabi United Group (Adug), an investment vehicle owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, a member of the Abu Dhabi royal family. Kogan has already pledged to resign if there is any political interference in any investigation the IFR may undertake into City, amid concerns it could create a diplomatic issue between the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates. Kogan’s comments came amid fresh scrutiny of Manchester City’s finances by the UK’s accounting watchdog. clusters.text: I always find major acquisitions more revealing than product launches. A launch can show where a company wants to go. A multi billion dollar deal shows where it believes it has to go. That makes this a busy week for Revenue Tech. Salesforce has agreed to acquire Braze for approximately $5.66 billion, while Intuit is buying Sequence and Robots & Pencils has acquired Tiger Pistol. The three deals sit in different parts of the market, but each is focused on a similar challenge: helping businesses turn more data into faster, more relevant commercial action. In other words, this is not just a rush to add AI features. It is a race to own the systems that help companies understand customer behavior, decide what to do next, and act across the revenue lifecycle. Salesforce Signs Agreement to Acquire Braze Salesforce has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Braze , a customer engagement platform, for approximately $5.66 billion in enterprise value. Braze helps marketers respond to customer behavior in real time across mobile apps, websites, email, SMS, WhatsApp, and other channels. Its platform continuously updates customer profiles and adapts customer journeys using live event data, while BrazeAI helps optimize content, offers, timing, and channels. If the deal closes, Salesforce expects Braze’s technology to strengthen Marketing Cloud across its wider platform, including Data 360, Customer 360, Agentforce, and SIForce. Salesforce has deep customer and commercial data, while Braze brings a proven way to use real-time behavioral signals to trigger personalized engagement at a very large scale. That matters as marketers face growing pressure to move beyond audience segments and scheduled campaigns. The ambition is to make each interaction more responsive to what a customer is doing in the moment, whether they are browsing, buying, or using a product. Patrick Stokes, President, Applications and Marketing at Salesforce , said: “Every interaction is an opportunity to wow your customers. Most of that wow comes from knowing your customer, and responding at just the right moment.” Braze serves around 2,770 customers, including Canva, Dairy Queen, Equinox, Instacart, Urban Outfitters, and Venmo.
